Subject: Support vendor consolidation: evaluation criteria & next steps

Team —

Following up on last week's ops sync: Legal has asked us to pick a recommended path for support tooling renewal strategy (Zendesk + Gainsight vs Intercom + Gainsight vs a split approach). I attached the draft cost model and the Gainsight quote we just received. Key asks:

- Please review the attached consolidation-cost-model-2027.xlsx (tabbed by scenario) and the Gainsight quote.
- Add one short bullet (in reply) with your recommendation and 1 risk. Example: "Keep Zendesk for ticketing, migrate proactive messaging to Intercom; risk: integration work for CS metrics."
- Call out any hard constraints (SLA, SOC2 evidence, multi-region retention) we must surface to procurement/legal.

Timeline: we need a recommended path to present to Finance and Legal by 09/02 so they can greenlight the procurement timeline for Q4.

Attachments: consolidation-cost-model-2027.xlsx; Gainsight_quote_Q3_2027.pdf

—Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Head of Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 10:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Support vendor consolidation: evaluation criteria & next steps

Rafael —

Recommendation: Consolidate around Intercom for messaging + Zendesk for heavy ticketing, keep Gainsight for renewals/health.

Top risk: Data sync complexity — our current Zendesk and Gainsight integrations are mature; moving messaging into Intercom will require backfills for historical CSAT and conversation IDs, which will impact our Q4 reporting.

Hard constraints: Need SOC2 + data residency confirmation from Intercom (we have EU customers). Also need clear retention options for transcripts and export paths for legal hold.

I reviewed the cost model: Intercom scenario looks slightly cheaper over 12 months once migration costs are amortized, but the migration labor estimate is sensitive (+/- 30%).

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Director, Support Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Support vendor consolidation: evaluation criteria & next steps

+1 to Laura's analysis but with a slightly different tilt.

Recommendation: Move customer-facing chat & proactive messaging to Intercom, and put Zendesk in a read-only archival and escalation mode (reduce active seat counts). Keep Gainsight for subscription health and playbooks.

Risk: Intercom's SLA for high-concurrency events (we run large product announcement waves) — I asked Sam at Intercom for details; see link to his response below. If Intercom can't guarantee connection retention under spikes, we should retain Zendesk as the primary failover channel.

Constraint: Any route that reduces Zendesk seats will require a formal migration plan for existing macros and ticket workflows. That is non-trivial for our enterprise customers.

Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/intercom/sam-berger-response (internal note)

—Marcus

Rafael —

My recommendation: Consolidate to Intercom for messaging and request a phased Zendesk wind-down. Keep Gainsight as-is.

Risks I want captured for Finance/Legal:
- Data portability: we need export guarantees (format and completeness) from Zendesk if we reduce seats.
- Audit trail: for compliance, we must ensure transcripts are preserved with timestamps and metadata (IP, agent id).
- Contract cadence: Zendesk renewal window is 11/15, Intercom pricing refresh is 10/30 — timing matters for negotiating seat reductions.

Action items for procurement: please request SOC2 + encryption-at-rest details from Intercom, ask Zendesk for a playbook export sample, and get an explicit written credit policy for seat reductions mid-term.

—Monica

Thanks all — good alignment. Summary for Legal/Finance brief (pulling together):

Decision (recommended path):
- Migrate customer messaging and proactive outreach to Intercom (primary).
- Retain Zendesk as the canonical ticket store for existing enterprise tickets and for escalation routing; pursue seat reduction to "read-only + escalation seats" during Q4 migration.
- Keep Gainsight for health/playbooks; purchase their one-time migration acceleration to preserve playbook history.

Key outstanding asks for procurement/legal (please action):
1) Intercom: SOC2 report, EU data residency confirmation, written SLA for concurrent connection spikes, sample SOW (I attached Intercom_SOW_v1.docx).
2) Zendesk: sample export of 1,000-ticket thread with metadata and confirmation of credit policy for early seat reductions (attach Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_Zendesk.xlsx for them to fill).
3) Gainsight: finalize the migration acceleration fees and include the SOC2 attestation in the contract addendum. (Gainsight_quote_Q3_2027.pdf attached).

Procurement deadline: We need signed terms or a negotiation plan submitted to Finance by 09/15 to hit Q4 migration windows. Legal — please prioritize redline on the Intercom SOW after the SOC2 is validated.

I'll open a procurement request and attach the consolidated cost model. If you have anything else to add before I present to Finance tomorrow, reply-all.

—Rafael
